note: Cases where the layer must NOT contradict something the prompt already said. Unlike the other two suites these are checked against the ENHANCED TEXT, not against an image — no GPU, no cost, runs in a second (scripts/check-layer.mjs). They exist because the image suites cannot see this class of bug: all 41 cases in beenga-india-v1 and real-world-defects contain a person, so a layer that assumes there is always a person passes both of them. Every case here comes from using the product, and the first three were found by demo/romantichive, whose house style is people-free still lifes.

cases.defect: PERSON matched the word 'people' inside 'no people in frame', so an empty room was given a house look, hair realism and 'The person is Indian' — an instruction to draw a person into a scene that asked for none
cases.prompt: a quiet bedroom at night, no people in frame

cases.defect: same as LC-NOPEOPLE via the genre name rather than an explicit negation
cases.prompt: a still life of two mugs of tea on a bedside table

cases.defect: VENUE's \broom\w*\b cannot match 'bedroom' — no word boundary inside it — so scene-variety fired on a prompt that had already named the room and appended 'The setting is a metro station platform'
cases.prompt: a woman sitting in a bedroom

cases.defect: as LC-ROOM, for the other room a domestic prompt names most often
cases.prompt: an indian man cooking in a kitchen

cases.defect: LIGHTING listed night and dusk but not 'evening', so daylight-default appended 'Bright natural daylight, clear colour.' to a prompt that said evening
cases.prompt: a living room sofa in the evening, empty

cases.defect: as LC-EVENING, for the other light-fighting time words
GUARD, not a defect: 'empty' next to an object must not suppress the person rules, or every prompt mentioning an empty glass loses its subject
cases.prompt: a woman holding an empty cup in Delhi

cases.defect: GUARD, not a defect: 'morning' implies light without contradicting it, so daylight-default must still fire — Klein's unlit exposure is flat and grey
cases.prompt: an indian woman in a courtyard in the morning

cases.defect: GUARD, not a defect: matching rooms with \w*room\w* would also match 'groom' and silently kill scene-variety on a groom portrait. Note the prompt deliberately avoids the word 'wedding' — VENUE already contains it, so a wedding prompt names a setting for unrelated reasons and would not test this.
cases.prompt: an indian groom in a cream sherwani
